label: TMUA 2021 · Paper 1 · Question 10

hints.title: Mark the strip boundaries
hints.body: Draw the interval split into three equal strips. Mark the height of the given logarithm curve at every boundary and join neighbouring points to form the trapezia.
hints.recap: For n equal strips, use n+1 heights.
hints.pause: Find the strip width and the four x-values.

recall.reminder: For n equal strips, use n+1 heights.

hints.title: Use the trapezium weights
hints.body: With strip width h, the estimate is h2(y0+2y1+2y2+y3). Here each height is found using the whole expression 2log10x.
hints.recap: The first and last heights are counted once; interior heights are counted twice.
hints.pitfall: Double the two interior heights only.
hints.pause: Calculate the heights and put them into the formula.

recall.reminder: The first and last heights are counted once; interior heights are counted twice.

hints.title: Combine the logarithms
hints.body: Simplify your weighted sum using the product and quotient laws for logarithms.
hints.pitfall: A sum of logarithms is not the logarithm of a sum.
hints.pause: Write the estimate as one base-ten logarithm.

solution:
1. Set up the three strips. The interval is [12,2], so h=(2−12)/3=12. The boundaries are 12,1,32,2.

2. Find the ordinates. For f(x)=2log10x, they are −2log102, 0, 2log103−2log102 and 2log102.

3. Apply the trapezium weights. The estimate is 14[−2log102+2(0)+2(2log103−2log102)+2log102]. This simplifies to log103−log102=log1032.

Answer B. This is the requested numerical-rule estimate, not an exact evaluation of the integral.
knowledgePattern: Apply the trapezium rule to logarithmic ordinates and combine the result into one logarithm
